summary: Narendra Nath Bhattacharyya was an Indology, religious studies, and history and archaeology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Kalikananda Avadhuta. He held a post at the University of Calcutta from circa 1967 to 1999.

Nariaki Nakazato is an Indology and history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1965 to 1974. He held posts at the CEACS (~1987–1993), Kobe University (~1993–1996), and the University of Tokyo (1999).

Philosopher Natalie Depraz studied at the ENS de lettres et sciences humaines (~1984–1988), Paris Nanterre University (1993), and St. Sergius Institute. She held posts at the Collège international de philosophie (1997), Paris-Sorbonne University (2000), and University of Rouen-Normandy (~2006).
Natalie Gummer is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who held posts at Harvard University and Beloit College (professor of religious studies, 2001).

Natalie Maxwell is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1970–1975) under Stephan Beyer. She also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Ngawang Lekden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Historian Natalie Rothman studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. She obtained a post at the University of Toronto in 2006.

Natasha Heller is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD from Harvard University (~1998–2005). She held positions at the University of California, Berkeley (~2005–2007) and the University of California, Los Angeles (~2007–2015).

Natasha Reichle is a Buddhist studies and history and archaeology scholar who completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley (~1995–2002) under Joanna Gottfried Williams, also studying with Amin Sweeney, Lewis Lancaster, Patricia Berger, Jeffrey Hadler, and Ninik Lunde.

Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen (2008–2018) under doctoral supervisor Hans T. Bakker, with Wout Jac. van Bekkum, Peter Bisschop, and Marijke J. Klokke on her committee.

Nathan Sivin was a Sinology and history scholar who studied at MIT, the Defense Language Institute, and Harvard. He held posts at MIT (~1966–1977), the University of Pennsylvania (~1977–2006), and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Nathan W. Hill is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Harvard University (~2001–2009) under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He held posts at SOAS University of London (~2008–2019) and Trinity College Dublin (2021).
Nathaniel Brassey Halhed was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Harrow School until circa 1768. He served as a Beamter at the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.

Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Virginia (~1997–2004) under Jeffrey Hopkins, having also studied under Khenpo Namdrol, David Germano, Karen C. Lang, and Richard Barnett.

Nathmal Tatia was an Indology, philosophy, and religious studies scholar who earned a DLitt at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He served as director at Jain Vishva Bharati Institute (~1991).

Navina Lamminger is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~2008–2013) under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard and committee member Jens-Uwe Hartmann.
Nawang Tsering Shakspo is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under doctoral supervisor Lal Mani Joshi. He served as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Neal Arvid Donner is a Sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia from circa 1971 to 1976 under Leon Hurvitz.
Neten Chokling Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure who studied under traditional teachers Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.

Ng-Fung Yuen is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of the West (~2004–2009) under Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, Joshua Capitanio, Zhihua Yao, Dan Lusthaus, Yikung, and Huaiyu Chen.

Ngan-che Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2007) under doctoral supervisor Jing Yin, alongside committee members K. L. Dhammajoti, Guang Xing, and Zhihua Yao.
